transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I’ve gotten into this habit of making myself throw up after I eat, and I can’t seem to stop doing it even though I know it’s not right. It's really hard for me to admit this out loud, but I just feel so stuck.
Do you feel very worried about gaining weight or feel like your self-worth is strongly tied to your body shape or weight?

Yes, I'm terrified of gaining weight; if the scale goes up even half a pound, I panic that I'm turning into an out-of-shape old lady. I pretty much judge my whole worth by how I look in my work coveralls next to the younger techs. If they feel tight or I look puffy, I feel like a complete failure who doesn't even deserve my lead tech spot.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F50.2", "F98.2"], but based on this conversation, F98.2 (atypical eating disorder of childhood or adolescence) is no longer likely because the patient's symptoms—such as intense fear of weight gain, self-worth tied to body shape, and recurrent purging behavior—are occurring in an adult context and align more specifically with a well-defined eating disorder typically seen in adults. The current presentation strongly supports F50.2 (bulimia nervosa), characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors like self-induced vomiting, along with excessive emphasis on body shape and weight in self-evaluation. No other differential diagnoses better account for the full clinical picture at this time.
